channel.title: The art of Kyle Parker Cunningham - line work
channel.description: Artist portfolio featuring painting, printmaking, and cinema

item.title: the atmosphere's electric finger
item.author: Unknown
item.description: Behold the awe which is the blinding light of lighting strikes when surrounded by the intense darkness of encroached clouds while miles away from domesticated electricity.

item.title: Astro Bee
item.author: Unknown
item.description: The intersection of space exploration and the natural world. An astronaut's helmet becomes a hive, bees navigating the cosmos within the human desire to explore beyond our atmosphere.

item.title: Bottled Oxygen
item.author: Unknown
item.description: Two bell jars share a hose: in one, a small yellow-leafed tree; in the other, a village of little dome houses, with a tap to meter the air between them. The tree works, the houses breathe. The future's utilities may be exactly this intimate.

item.title: Dayhike
item.author: Unknown
item.description: A songbird with a backpack, ready for the trail (the plate is scratched 2018). The owl pioneered the look in 2016; word spreads fast in the forest.

item.title: Elephant Mask
item.author: Unknown
item.description: Behind the bright yellow elephant mask: an elephant. "We all wear masks most of the time," the painting said back in 2018 — and the most convincing disguise is always yourself, slightly off.

item.title: In The Pines
item.author: Unknown
item.description: Six pines, hand colored in six different greens, standing in their own quiet. Named for the place where shadows stack vertical and the needles make their own floor — and maybe a little for the old song.

item.title: Thread
item.author: Unknown
item.description: Intaglio drypoint prints. Printed area approx 6 x 9 inches. Handtorn paper approx 8 x 10 inches. Line work describes an angular hand on the right pulling a string emerging from the left vertical edge of the print.

item.title: Abduction
item.author: Unknown

item.title: Olympus
item.author: Unknown
item.description: This is one of my favorite typewriters of all time. Unfortunately it has a sticky "n" key, it works, but you get some type errors. That, though, is the cost of being analog!

item.title: Origami Beetroot
item.author: Unknown
item.description:
A beet pulled and drawn like a botanical plate, its leaves creased flat and angular as folded paper. The garden produces its own origami; you just have to pull it up and turn it over.

Intaglio Drypoint Print.

item.title: Submerged
item.author: Unknown
item.description: A diver stands on the bottom, helmet line wandering all the way up to the thin band of the surface. Sibling of Deep Sea (2018) — the same predicament, revisited.

item.title: Space Owl
item.author: Unknown
item.description:
The owl, helmeted, antenna up. The owls already hold their conversations across the night (Saturday Evening Owls eavesdrops on them); this one has simply extended the broadcast range.

Intaglio drypoint prints. Printed area approx 6 x 9 inches. Handtorn paper approx 8 x 10 inches.

item.title: vacation
item.author: Unknown
item.description:
A figure stands easy on green ground in a gold space helmet, oxygen tank resting at the knee. A vacation in the future may require equipment, but the posture is eternal: shoulders down, nowhere to be, air supply secured.

intaglio drypoint prints printed area approx 6 x 9 inches handtorn paper approx 8 x 10 inches

Each print is printed in an open ended series. I physically scratch the print number into the plate before inking it and then print just one copy at that number.

item.title: Path Through the Autumn Leaves
item.author: Unknown
item.description:
Concentric squares in the colors of fall — orange, rust, a thread of turquoise sky — narrowing toward a small bright center. The sibling of Autumnal Twilight's circles: the same walk through the same season, this time with corners. A path is just a square spiral you follow inward until the leaves close over the way you came.

Oil on Linen. 17 1/2 by 17 1/2 inches. 2021.

item.title: expansion drypoint
item.author: Unknown
item.description:
The mind shifts color pretending the future is a peeled orange imitating a banana.

8 x 10 inches paper Rives BFK

item.title: owl
item.author: Unknown
item.description:
oil on baltic birch panel 12x17.5 inches painted 2012, reworked spring 2021

This painting was from a few years ago. I reworked this painting in April 2021 to how it is here.

I have mixed feelings about working on old paintings. On the one hand I love the old paintings, they have a piece of history of my life in them, they were a time and a place and they represent what I was capable of doing and what I was thinking at that moment. On the other hand I'm an infinitely better painter now than I ever have been. This owl, now, has more of my history representing it's form, owls are magical and deserve to look as good as possible.

item.title: Alligator Juniper
item.author: Unknown
item.description:
The Nogal Canyon juniper, wind-bent and holding on. The third alligator juniper in the series — they are the great elders of this country, and I keep visiting them with a scribe point the way you visit grandparents with a camera. See also Nogal Canyon (2022).

Intaglio drypoint prints. Printed area approx 6 x 9 inches, handtorn paper approx 8 x 10 inches.

item.title: Alligator Juniper
item.author: Unknown
item.description:
The juniper again, this time at arm's length: the trunk and limbs filling the frame, bark in checkered plates like reptile hide. You can know a tree from across the mesa or from inside its shade; this is the second kind of knowing.

intaglio printmaking on rives bfk. 8 by 10 inches. 2018. private collection.

item.title: Space Worm
item.author: Unknown
item.description: intaglio drypoint prints. printed area approx 6 x 9 inches. handtorn paper approx 8 x 10 inches.

item.title: 120 Volts
item.author: Unknown
item.description:
A long, stooped figure plugged into the wall outlet by his own hair. Household current as life support, five years before the sky demonstrated the high-voltage version on me personally. The glitch of daily reality at its most literal: we are all on the grid.

intaglio printmaking on rives bfk. 8 by 10 inches. 2018.

item.title: Deep Sea
item.author: Unknown
item.description:
A figure in a diving helmet stands on the bottom, while a single line wanders all the way up to the thin green-and-red band of the surface, impossibly far above. Some days are like that. The air is up there somewhere.

8 x 10 inches. Drypoint Intaglio Print. Handcolored with watercolor. 2018.

item.title: Aeropress
item.author: Unknown
item.description:
The Aeropress, drawn like the small monument it is — exploded view, chambers stacked. Part of the coffee congregation, with the carafe and the espresso machine. 2018 plate #1 — the year started properly.

intaglio printmaking on rives bfk. 8 by 10 inches. 2018. private collection.

item.title: Air Lift
item.author: Unknown
item.description:
Two hot air balloons cooperate to lift one untroubled elephant. The first appearance of an airlift I kept returning to — the plate was pulled again in 2021. Some problems simply require more balloons.

5 x 7 inches. Drypoint Intaglio Print. Spring 2016.

item.title: Boom Box
item.author: Unknown
item.description:
A skull-faced figure in a space helmet carries a boombox on one shoulder, walking the horizon line. Every era gets the procession it deserves; ours brings its own soundtrack and its own helmet.

5 x 7 inches. Drypoint Intaglio Print. Spring 2016.

item.title: Day Hike
item.author: Unknown
item.description:
An owl wearing a backpack, ready for the trail. The work of a day hike is mostly looking — and nobody looks like an owl. A backpacked songbird took up the same hobby in Dayhike (2023).

5 x 7 inches. Drypoint Intaglio Print. Spring 2016.

item.title: Alligator Juniper (Adobe Canyon)
item.author: Unknown
item.description:
A whole alligator juniper, drawn limb by limb, the checkered bark that names the species rendered scratch by scratch. The drypoint scribe turns out to be the right tool for a tree that grows one century at a time.

8 x 10 inches. Intaglio Drypoint Print. Spring 2016. private collection.

item.title: Expansion
item.author: Unknown
item.description:
The mind shifts color pretending the future is a pealed orange imitating a banana.

Six by Seven Inches. Oil on Handwoven Linen. Summer 2014.
